text:
10. None of the photographs shown shall be destroyed, whether or not an identification is
made, since they may be required for production in court. The photographs shall be
numbered and a separate photograph taken of the frame or part of the album from which
the eye-witness made an identification as an aid to reconstituting it.
(b) Documentation

11. Whether or not an identification is made, a record shall be kept of the showing of
photographs on forms provided for the purpose. This shall include anything said by the
eye-witness about any identification or the conduct of the procedure, any reasons it was not
practicable to comply with any of the provisions of this Code governing the showing of
photographs and the name and rank of the supervising officer.

12. The supervising officer shall inspect and sign the record as soon as practicable.
